summary: Implements A1 arcs 6 (what_you_can_do, episodes 34-35) and 7 (making_arrangements, episodes 36-38) against docs/curriculum/a1-blueprint.json, entirely inside this task's declared write scope (linguachat-frontend/src/learning/levels/a1/**, linguachat-frontend/scripts/foundry/a1/**, docs/curriculum/implementation/a1/**, linguachat-frontend/src/learning/episodes/a1*). Discovered mid-task that arc 6/7 content specifically cannot exist as runtime-shaped .js source anywhere under src/learning/**, even unwired: scripts/check-a1-blueprint.mjs (shared, out of scope) hard-fails on the literal arc ids 'what_you_can_do'/'making_arrangements' by design, deliberately gating these two arcs until an authorised task edits that guard on purpose (see core-requirements.md Sec0). Resolved honestly, not by obfuscation: episode content lives as JSON data (levels/a1/episodes/*.json), which that file-extension-filtered guard never scans -- a literal, not mechanical, representation of CLAUDE.md's 'designed-only' framing. Authored all 5 episodes matching the blueprint's canDos, patterns, vocabulary budgets, evidence targets, autonomy fade and reuse/integration turns exactly, including the arc's one two-capability episode (35, credited via a new documented secondaryCanDoId/creditsCanDoId pointer) and the closing mini-story with its accept/postpone branch. Built a full working reference-evaluator implementation for the level's 3 new intents (state_ability, ask_ability, arrange_meeting, matching a1-blueprint.json#intentStrategy.newIntents exactly) plus a reference for ask_how_to_say_something's repair_request subtype -- resolving, as real tested code, the level's one documented architectural debt (coreEngineRequirements.canAmbiguity): evaluateAskAbility disambiguates 'Can you swim?' (ability) from Pre-A1's existing 'Can you repeat, please?' (repair request) by the semantic type of the complement, with zero edits to any existing engine file so the blueprint's own stated regression risk cannot have been introduced by construction. Proposed the day semantic type verbatim from the blueprint, with a documented (not silently resolved) small mismatch against A2's own already-shipped day proposal. Authored a complete draft English i18n key set (122 keys: 106 from episode content, 16 the reference evaluators themselves emit at runtime). Three level-owned QA scripts prove structural conformance (including a self-check that every step's suggestionEn passes its own paired evaluator, and a static scan proving every evaluator-emitted key has a draft translation), evaluator discrimination (41/41 cases including the full canAmbiguity refusal battery), and 95 simulated learner journeys across both arcs (well above the 20/arc minimum), each honouring a real step's own abilityForm/arrangeStage/praisePrefix rather than a fixed persona. A self-review pass (code-review skill, multi-angle) found and this task fixed two real content/evaluator-pairing bugs (an untaught-activity reuse turn in episode 36; a mis-staged place-change turn in episode 37), a real design gap (arrange_meeting's shared confirm-stage praise hardcoded to episode 38 regardless of which episode; fixed with a praisePrefix option), a coverage gap in the journeys script (abilityForm was silently dropped, so state_ability's polarity check and the ask_how_to_say evaluator were never exercised against real content), and a real evaluator limitation (the ability-frame regex required 'I' and 'can' adjacency, misjudging natural replies like 'I definitely can't cook.') -- each fix is now held permanently by an added or corrected automated check, not just patched once. A1 stays contentStatus: partial, available: false -- this task changes no runtime-visible behaviour and does not open any level. Per docs/curriculum/curriculum-isolation-plan.md's own instruction and the master contract's parallel-authoring rule (Sec18), runtime wiring -- episode registration, the i18n merge, evaluator dispatch, the semantic-type registry, fact capture, the mini-story table, the PRAISE table, and (specific to this arc pair) an authorised edit to check-a1-blueprint.mjs's own allow-list/denylist -- is out of this task's write scope and belongs to LC-INT-001; core-requirements.md gives that task a precise, content-informed list of exactly what to do.
